svg.title: My AgentRig to Trinary Agents workflow shift
svg.desc: A dark side-by-side comparison. The earlier AgentRig setup uses an installed CLI, scripts launching headless agent processes, SQLite workflow state committed to Git, and a status board. Trinary Agents uses a skill in the host, the main agent as project manager, host-managed worker and reviewer sub-agents, Markdown task and handoff records, and a generated read-only dashboard. A note explains that current AgentRig has evolved with Markdown storage and planner-managed sub-agents.
svg.text: Same team pattern. Different boundary of responsibility.
Earlier setup shown on the left; the skill-first path I use on the right.
AgentRig · my earlier setup
Trinary Agents · skill-first workflow
Installed CLI + configured workspace
Profiles, task commands, agent launch and status
Planner / controller
My earlier scripts started headless worker and reviewer CLIs
SQLite workflow state
Tasks + handoffs; committed snapshots gave recovery points
CLI status + read-only task board
Useful visibility, with the CLI/database as workflow machinery
Skill installed in the agent host
Carries the roles, rules, gates and file conventions
Main agent is project manager
Host launches a worker, then a separate reviewer sub-agent
Markdown is canonical workflow state
Approved plan · task status/dependencies · append-only handoffs
Generated dashboard is a read-only view
Rebuild from Markdown; it never owns task status
A note on the projects today
AgentRig has since added planner-managed sub-agents and selectable Markdown storage; this compares my earlier setup with Trinary's narrower skill-first path.
